newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures firm after uneventful G7.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures firm after uneventful G7.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures firmed slightly on Monday with dealers saying sentiment had benefited from an uneventful Group of Seven (G7) meeting.

"The G7 gave us no surprises, nothing special," said one local futures dealer. There had been worries that the United States might put pressure on Japan at the summit in Denver over the Japanese trade surplus.
By the lunchtime break, the Nikkei 225 September contract was 30 points higher at 20,490 on volume of 3,080.
Dealers said the contract appeared to be in the middle of a 300-point trading range between 20,350 and 20,650.
"It's quiet, consolidating -- safe and secure above 20,000," said a dealer who follows chart analysis.
The dealer said the only possible blot on the landscape in the immediate future was the weakness of the yen, which had slipped to around 115.50 to the dollar by mid-morning.
"If it weakens much more, that would be negative for stocks," said the dealer.
The June MSCI Taiwan index contract stood at ended at 382.0 on volume of 410 lots by 0245 GMT.
